title: THE CORIOLIS DEFLECTION
narration_text: Global winds do not blow in straight lines. Because Earth rotates on its axis, moving air is deflected by the Coriolis Effect. In the Northern Hemisphere, winds curve to the right, spinning cyclonic storms counter-clockwise. In the Southern Hemisphere, they deflect to the left, creating clockwise rotation. This atmospheric rotation dictates everything from local hurricane pathways to the massive trade winds that cross our oceans.
